answer: Admission sits at the domain layer: a verifier named ZoneSeal resolves a signed TXT record in its zone, walks the DNSSEC chain to root, and checks the RDAP registrant handle against a registry refusing any handle already bound to a seat. The penalty trigger is a duplicate handle or two seats behind one registrar account, burning both bonds. A domain costs twelve dollars yearly and verification five, so N fakes cost N times seventeen dollars plus N propagation waits. A copied record splits like a prism, a shared handle sinks the reef, and no proxy reaches the zenith of a clean zone.
